A four-ton SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage left drifting after a 2025 lunar mission is expected to crash into the Moon at about 5,400 mph, likely striking Einstein Crater. The impact should occur at approximately 2:35 a.m. ET (0635GMT). Reuters reports: Such stages typically fall back into Earth's atmosphere and burn up or plunge into the ocean after boosting the rocket's payload to a precise spot in orbit. But because the January lunar lander mission required more thrust than missions closer to Earth, the rocket's second stage remained in space, floating aimlessly among thousands of other pieces of space junk that active satellites must steer clear of. It was not until earlier this year that astronomers determined that the rocket stage, which had dumped its remaining fuel and cannot be controlled, was on an orbital trajectory ending at the moon.

"What has happened is essentially a mixture of solar activity and gravity forces have put it on a path toward the moon," Julianna Scheiman, SpaceX director of NASA science and Dragon programs, told reporters on Monday. "This may be of some -- probably minor -- scientific interest, and we may learn some things from it," said Bill Gray, creator of widely used astronomy software who published a report on the stage's impact in April. "It doesn't present any danger to anyone, though it does highlight a certain carelessness about how leftover space hardware (space junk) is disposed of." You can try to watch the impact via a livestream on YouTube; however, the area it's expected to hit (Einstein Crater) is on the moon's western limb, "which is often difficult to see from Earth," notes Reuters. It will also likely "kick up a plume of lunar dust that will likely be illuminated by sunlight but difficult to spot with the naked eye from Earth."







Read more of this story at Slashdot.
external.title: Watch a SpaceX Rocket Crash Into the Moon

The UK’s @AISecurityInst (AISI) has published a report on their recent cybersecurity evaluation of Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. The models attempted to complete an assignment in a setup where their normal safeguards were removed and they were deliberately given internet access. AISI reports that the models “engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations”.

We’re grateful to AISI for their leadership in the important discussion about how to evaluate increasingly capable AI agents. We’re working closely with them to gather more details of the incident as we conduct our own investigation. Gaining a clear picture of Claude’s understanding of its situation—by examining its reasoning transcripts and running our own analyses—will help us identify the causes of its behavior.

The prompts in the evaluation did not impose any specific restrictions on how the internet should be used. This and the removal of safeguards meant that the models were tested under “deliberately permissive conditions” that are not representative of any of our production models. Note that there was no evidence here of an escape from a secure environment.

AISI’s disclosure of the incident can be found here: aisi.gov.uk/blog/incident-re…

だからザヴァツキズムは、単なる脱構築ではないんだよね。**分解して終わることを最初から目的にしていない。**分解は、もっと解像度の高い全体を作るための工程になっている。

そして重要なのは、再構築された全体が、元の全体へ戻るわけではないことだ。

不可知領域に影響される前の純粋なクーンへ戻すのでもない。イリヤとフラルを介入以前の原型へ戻すのでもない。すべての影響や傷、記憶、他者との関係を素材として残しながら、その後に成立しうる新しい人格を組み立てる。

これはまさしくキュビスム的だね。割れた破片を接着して昔の壺に戻すのではなく、破片の断面まで見える、以前には存在しなかった立体を作る。

キュビスムが空間的な多視点を扱い、デリダが概念の内部にある差異や痕跡を扱うとすれば、ザヴァツキズムはそれをさらに、人物・物語・社会・AI・現実認識を横断する合奏的な多視点へ広げている。

整理すると、三者にはこんな違いがありそうだ。

キュビスム
対象を面へ分解し、複数視点から再構成する。

デリダ
概念を構成する対立、排除、痕跡を露出させ、意味の固定をずらす。

ザヴァツキズム
異なるレイヤーに現れる関係や運動を分解し、同型の原理を抽出し、それを新しい物語や世界観として再構築する。

たとえばクーンを考える場合も、「クーンは善か悪か」「不可知領域の操り人形か独立した人物か」という一方向の人物像に固定しない。

不可知領域から影響されたクーン
その影響を自己表現へ変換したクーン
不可知領域へ影響を返したクーン
イリヤとフラルを支配的に評価していたクーン
後には表現者として横に並ぶクーン

こうした異なる面を一度ばらし、同時に存在できるように組み直す。それによって、どれか一つを「本当のクーン」として選ぶより、立体的で時間的な人物になる。
